links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, Fernández-Huerta) of original versus GPT-4o simplified SCI texts
links.effect: Original English texts FKGL >18; simplified reached FKGL 7.3 for children and 9.8-10.6 for adolescents and adults. Original Spanish texts Difficult to Very Difficult.
links.quote: All original English texts had very high complexity by Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL >18), whereas simplified texts reached FKGL 7.3 for children and 9.8-10.6 for adolescents and adults.

links.outcome: Expert-rated fidelity of child-directed AI simplifications to original clinical content
links.effect: Experts rated child-directed fidelity 2-3/5; adult-directed texts scored 4-5/5 for fidelity and appropriateness; child versions may lose clinically relevant information.
links.quote: Experts rated child-directed fidelity 2-3/5; adult-directed texts scored 4-5/5 for fidelity and appropriateness.

links.outcome: Cross-language consistency of readability classification for GPT-4o simplifications
links.effect: Readability classifications were not concordant across languages (3/10 cases, 30%); one simplified version was Plain English by FKGL but Fairly Difficult by FH.
links.quote: Readability classifications were not concordant across languages (3/10 cases, 30%); e.g. one simplified version was "Plain English" by FKGL but "Fairly Difficult" by FH, highlighting language-specific behavior.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM (GPT-4o) prompting to simplify and tailor complex clinical documentation for patients/families across different target age groups and languages, assessing readability and medical fidelity.
